mr001.tt:
This is a composition written by Lin.

Japanese baths
Lin

I came to Japan last month. Now I live in the house of a Japanese family.
On the night I arrived in Japan, the mother said, "Please take a bath." In my country, everyone just takes showers. We rarely take baths. The bath water was very hot, so I only stayed in for a little while.
But now I love baths. Every night I soak for about 30 minutes. When I take a bath, I can sleep well.

qs.e: おゆは とても あつかったですから.
qs.t: Why did Lin only stay in the bath for a little while?

qs.e: いまは おふろが だいすきです.
qs.t: What does Lin think of baths now?

mr002.tt:
This is a composition written by Mike.

My weekend
Mike

Last Saturday I went to the mountains with my friend Ken. We met at the station at 6 a.m. and rode the train for two hours.
The mountain was very high. While climbing, I got tired and rested many times. Ken said, "It's fine to go slowly," and waited for me.
At the top of the mountain, the two of us ate our packed lunches. The town seen from the top looked very small and beautiful. Next time I want to go again in autumn.

qs.e: ゆっくりで いいですよと いって、まって くれました.
qs.t: What did Ken do while they were climbing the mountain?

qs.e: こんどは あきに また いきたいです.
qs.t: When does Mike want to go to the mountains next time?

mr003.tt:
This is a composition written by Anna.

My part-time job
Anna

I have a part-time job at a bakery near my university. I work on Monday, Wednesday and Friday mornings, from 7 to 10.
At first I couldn't remember the names of the breads, and it was hard. But the manager kindly taught me. Now I know them all.
After work, the manager always gives me the leftover bread. I eat it for lunch.

qs.e: Mon, Wed, Fri: 3 times.
qs.t: How many times a week does Anna work?

qs.e: それ = のこった パン.
qs.t: What does "it" (それ) refer to?

mr004.tt:
This is a composition written by Chen.

My first Japanese
Chen

In my country I often watched Japanese anime. That made me want to study Japanese.
Since April last year, I've been going to a Japanese language school. At first kanji were difficult, and I cried every day. When I told my classmates, they said, "It was the same for me. If you learn a little every day, you'll be fine."
Now I learn five kanji every day. I've also started to understand anime a little.

qs.e: アニメを よく みて いました。それで…
qs.t: Why did Chen want to study Japanese?

qs.e: まいにち すこしずつ おぼえれば だいじょうぶ.
qs.t: What did Chen's friends say to him?

mr005.tt:
This is a composition written by Sara.

My family
Sara

There are four people in my family: my father, my mother, my younger brother and me. My father is a doctor and is always busy. My mother is an elementary school teacher. My brother is a high school student and is good at soccer.
I'm studying in Japan now, so I can't see my family. But we talk on the phone every Sunday. My brother always talks about soccer.
During the summer holidays, I want to go back to my country and see everyone.

qs.e: ははは しょうがっこうの せんせいです.
qs.t: What is Sara's mother's job?

qs.e: まいしゅう にちようびに でんわで はなします.
qs.t: When does Sara talk with her family?

mr006.tt:
This is a composition written by Tom.

Something I left behind
Tom

Yesterday I left my bag on the train. In the bag were my wallet and a Japanese book.
I told a station worker right away. The station worker called other stations for me. After waiting about 30 minutes, the station worker said, "We found your bag. It's at the next station."
I went to the next station and got my bag. The money in my wallet and the book were all there. I thought Japan is really amazing.

qs.e: つぎの えきに あります.
qs.t: Where was the bag?

qs.e: おかねも ほんも ぜんぶ ありました.
qs.t: Why did Tom think it was "amazing"?

mr007.tt:
This is a composition written by Han.

My favorite restaurant
Han

There is a small ramen shop near my house. It's run by an old man and an old woman. The shop is old, but the ramen is very delicious.
The first time I went, I didn't understand much Japanese. I couldn't read the menu either. The old woman showed me pictures and explained slowly.
Now I go to that shop once a week. I also look forward to talking with the old woman.

qs.e: しゃしんを みせて、ゆっくり せつめいして くれました.
qs.t: What did the old woman do the first time Han went?

qs.e: しゅうに １かい.
qs.t: How often does Han go to that shop?

mr008.tt:
This is a composition written by Emma.

Summer in Japan
Emma

Summer in my country is cool. But summer in Japan is very hot, and I was surprised. In July and August it was about 35 degrees every day.
On hot days, I turned on the air conditioner at home and drank lots of cold things. When I went out, I wore a hat.
But there are good things about summer in Japan, too: fireworks. In August I watched fireworks by the river with friends. They were very beautiful.

qs.e: エアコンを つけて、つめたい ものを たくさん のみました.
qs.t: What did Emma do on hot days?

qs.e: いい こと: はなび.
qs.t: For Emma, what is good about summer in Japan?

mr009.tt:
This is a composition written by John.

Cooking class
John

I'm bad at cooking. In my country my mother always cooked for me. After I came to Japan, I ate convenience store boxed lunches every day.
Since last month, I've been going to a cooking class once a week. The teacher is Japanese and teaches us Japanese cooking. Last week we made miso soup.
Now I sometimes cook at home too. Next time my mother comes to Japan, I want her to eat food I made.

qs.e: まいにち コンビニの おべんとうを たべて いました.
qs.t: What was John eating when he came to Japan?

qs.e: ははに わたしが つくった りょうりを たべて もらいたい.
qs.t: What does John want to do from now on?

mr010.tt:
This is a composition written by Min.

My town
Min

I now live in a small town near Tokyo. There's no big department store in the town, but there are supermarkets and a hospital near the station, so it's convenient.
My apartment is a 15-minute walk from the station. It's a little far, but I can see the mountains from my apartment window. I like looking at them in the morning.
On weekends I go to Tokyo by train and go shopping. It's 40 minutes to Tokyo by train.

qs.e: まどから やまが みえます。それを みるのが すき.
qs.t: What does "them" (それ) refer to?

qs.e: おおきい デパートは ありません.
qs.t: What doesn't Min's town have?

mr011.tt:
This is a composition written by Louis.

Rainy days
Louis

In Japan it rains a lot in June. I used to hate the rain, because my shoes get wet and I can't ride my bicycle.
One rainy day, on my way home from school, I left my umbrella on the train. While I was at the station not knowing what to do, an old woman I didn't know said, "Let's go together," and let me under her umbrella. She walked with me all the way to my house.
Since that day, I've come to like rainy days a little.

qs.e: くつが ぬれるし、じてんしゃに のる ことが できないから.
qs.t: Why did Louis hate the rain?

qs.e: かさに いれて くれました。いえまで いっしょに あるいて くれました.
qs.t: What did the old woman do?

mr012.tt:
This is a composition written by Nana.

My dog
Nana

We have a dog named Pochi. Pochi is 10 years old and already an old dog.
We used to run together to the park every morning. But now he can't run much. So we take slow walks near our house.
Pochi loves meat. But the vet said, "Please don't give him much meat." Sometimes I give him just a little. Then Pochi looks very happy.

qs.e: いまは いえの ちかくを ゆっくり さんぽします.
qs.t: What does Nana do with Pochi now?

qs.e: にくを あまり たべさせないで ください.
qs.t: What did the vet say?

mr013.tt:
This is a composition written by Kate.

My birthday
Kate

Last Friday was my birthday. It was my first birthday in Japan, so I thought I would be a little lonely.
That day, when I got to school, the classroom lights were off. I thought it was strange and turned on the lights, and everyone in the class said, "Happy birthday!" There was a cake on the desk.
I was so happy that I cried a little.

qs.e: すこし さびしいと おもって いました.
qs.t: Before her birthday, how did Kate feel?

qs.e: みんなが おめでとうと いいました。ケーキが ありました.
qs.t: What happened in the classroom?

mr014.tt:
This is a composition written by Park.

My mornings
Park

I'm not good with mornings. Even when the alarm clock rings, I just can't get up. Because of that, I was late for school three times last month.
My teacher told me, "Try putting your alarm clock somewhere far from your bed." I put the clock near the door of my room. To stop the clock, I have to get out of bed.
This was a good method. This month I haven't been late even once yet.

qs.e: とけいを へやの ドアの ちかくに おきました.
qs.t: What does "this" (これ) refer to?

qs.e: こんげつは まだ いちども おくれて いません.
qs.t: How many times was Park late for school this month?

mr015.tt:
This is a composition written by Yi.

The library
Yi

I often go to the city library. It's in front of the station and is open from Monday to Saturday.
The library has not only Japanese books but also Korean books. I like reading books from my country, so I often borrow them.
You can borrow up to five books at a time. You have to return them within two weeks.

qs.e: くにの ほん = かんこくごの ほん.
qs.t: What does "them" (それ) refer to?

qs.e: ２しゅうかんで かえさなければ なりません.
qs.t: Which statement about this library is correct?

mr016.tt:
This is a composition written by Ali.

My first snow
Ali

In my country it's hot all year round, so it doesn't snow. In January this year, I saw snow for the first time in Japan.
That morning, when I opened the window, everything outside was white. I went outside right away and touched the snow. It was very cold.
After that, I made a snowman in the park with friends. In the evening I sent a photo of the snowman to my family. They were very surprised.

qs.e: すぐ そとへ でて、ゆきに さわりました.
qs.t: After opening the window, what did Ali do first?

qs.e: ゆきだるまの しゃしんを おくりました。かぞくは びっくりして いました.
qs.t: Why was his family surprised?

mr017.tt:
This is a composition written by Carlos.

Japanese trains
Carlos

Japanese trains are very quiet. Nobody talks on the phone on the train. Everyone is reading books or sleeping. Trains in my country are noisy, and everyone talks loudly.
The first time I rode a Japanese train, I talked loudly with a friend. The people around us looked at us. I was embarrassed.
Now I'm quiet on the train.

qs.e: ほんを よんだり、ねたり して います.
qs.t: What are people doing on Japanese trains?

qs.e: おおきい こえで はなして、まわりの ひとが みました.
qs.t: Why was Carlos embarrassed?

mr018.tt:
This is a composition written by Maria.

The festival
Maria

Last Saturday there was a festival at the shrine near my house. My Japanese friend Yumi invited me: "Let's go together."
Yumi lent me a yukata. Putting on a yukata was difficult, but Yumi's mother helped me.
There were many stalls at the festival. I ate yakisoba and shaved ice. The shaved ice was cold and very delicious. I want to go again next year.

qs.e: ゆみさんは わたしに ゆかたを かして くれました.
qs.t: Who lent Maria the yukata?

qs.e: やきそばと かきごおりを たべました.
qs.t: What did Maria do at the festival?

mr019.tt:
This is a composition written by Paul.

Studying Japanese
Paul

Every morning I study Japanese on the train. It's 40 minutes by train from my house to the office, so I can study for 40 minutes every day.
From Monday to Wednesday I study kanji, and on Thursdays and Fridays I listen to the radio in Japanese. On weekends I don't take the train, so I don't study.
I have a Japanese exam in December. I want to do my best.

qs.e: もくようびと きんようびは ラジオを ききます.
qs.t: What does Paul do on Thursdays?

qs.e: しゅうまつは でんしゃに のりませんから.
qs.t: Why doesn't Paul study on weekends?

mr020.tt:
This is a composition written by Smith.

Moving
Smith

Last month I moved to a new apartment. My old apartment was far from the station, and the room was small.
The new apartment is a three-minute walk from the station. The room is spacious and bright. But the rent is higher than at my old apartment.
On moving day, three people from my company came to help. After the move, we all ate pizza together.

qs.e: まえの アパートより やちんが たかい.
qs.t: Which statement about the new apartment is correct?

qs.e: ともだちが ３にん.
qs.t: On moving day, how many people came to help?

mr021.tt:
This is a composition written by Yuki.

My grandmother
Yuki

My grandmother is 80 years old, but she is very healthy. Every morning she gets up at 5 and waters the flowers in the garden.
My grandmother is a very good cook. I like her tempura best. Last year she taught me how to make tempura. But when I make it, it doesn't come out as delicious as hers.
During the next holidays, I plan to go to my grandmother's house and make it together.

qs.e: にわの はなに みずを やります.
qs.t: What does the grandmother do every morning?

qs.e: Her tempura doesn't turn out as delicious as her grandmother's.
qs.t: What does "it doesn't come out as delicious as hers" mean?

mr022.tt:
This is a composition written by Dan.

Japanese schools
Dan

I teach English at a Japanese high school. There is something about Japanese schools that surprised me.
Japanese students clean their classrooms themselves after class. In my country, students don't clean; there are people whose job is cleaning.
At first I thought it was strange. But now I think it's very good, because when you clean it yourself, you start taking care of the classroom.

qs.e: じぶんたちで きょうしつを そうじします.
qs.t: What surprised Dan at the Japanese school?

qs.e: いまは とても いいと おもいます.
qs.t: What does Dan think about the cleaning now?

mr023.tt:
This is a composition written by Jean.

Japanese convenience stores
Jean

Japanese convenience stores are very convenient. They sell not only food and drinks, but you can also buy stamps and postcards. You can even pay your electricity bill.
Every morning, before going to the office, I buy coffee at the convenience store. The staff always say "Good morning" to me. That makes me happy.
Shops in my country close at 9 p.m., but Japanese convenience stores are open at night too.

qs.e: それ = 「おはようございます」と いう こと.
qs.t: What does "that" (それ) refer to?

qs.e: They close at 9.
qs.t: What are shops like in Jean's country?

mr024.tt:
This is a composition written by Mei.

My first job
Mei

Since last month I've had a part-time job at a restaurant. I work twice a week, on Saturdays and Sundays.
The first day was very hard. The customers spoke Japanese very fast, and I couldn't understand them well. On top of that, I broke a plate.
But everyone at the restaurant is very kind, and they said, "Don't worry about it." Now I enjoy the work.

qs.e: Saturday and Sunday.
qs.t: When does Mei work?

qs.e: The customers spoke Japanese fast.
qs.t: Why was the first day hard?

mr025.tt:
This is a composition written by Luca.

My bicycle
Luca

Right after I came to Japan, I bought a bicycle. I ride it to school, to go shopping, and so on. It's cheaper and faster than the bus.
But last week I parked my bicycle in front of the station, and it disappeared. It was a place where parking wasn't allowed. I went to city hall, paid 2,000 yen, and got my bicycle back.
Now I park it properly in the bicycle parking lot.

qs.e: He parked it where it wasn't allowed.
qs.t: Why did the bicycle disappear?

qs.e: He paid 2,000 yen at city hall.
qs.t: What did Luca do to get his bicycle back?

mr026.tt:
This is a composition written by Hana.

My weekend
Hana

On Saturdays I always get up early and go to the market. The vegetables and fish at the market are fresh and cheaper than at the supermarket.
I make lunch with the fish I buy at the market. In the afternoon I play tennis in the park with a friend.
On Sundays I don't go anywhere. I clean and do laundry at home, and go to bed early at night.

qs.e: Fresher and cheaper.
qs.t: Why does Hana go to the market?

qs.e: Housework.
qs.t: What does Hana do on Sundays?

mr027.tt:
This is a composition written by Tom.

The Japanese exam
Tom

I'm taking a Japanese exam in December. I study a little every day.
In the morning I learn five kanji. During my lunch break I listen to the radio in Japanese. At night I do 20 grammar questions.
The most difficult thing is listening, because Japanese people speak fast. But I understand a little more than last month.

qs.e: He listens to the radio.
qs.t: What does Tom do during his lunch break?

qs.e: Listening.
qs.t: What is the most difficult thing for Tom?

mr028.tt:
This is a composition written by An.

My friend's house
An

Last Sunday I went to a Japanese friend's house. When I went into the house, I took off my shoes. In my country we wear shoes even inside the house, so I was a little surprised.
My friend's mother made us tempura. It was so delicious that I asked her to teach me how to make it.
Next time I want to invite my friend to my house and cook food from my country.

qs.e: Taking off shoes.
qs.t: Why was An surprised?

qs.e: Cooking food from her country.
qs.t: What does An want to do next time?

mr029.tt:
This is a composition written by Ken.

My room
Ken

My room is on the third floor of an apartment building. It's small, but the window is big, so it's bright.
In my room there is a bed, a desk and a bookshelf. There is no TV. I watch the news on my smartphone.
There is one thing that bothers me: there's no elevator, so it's very hard when I carry heavy things.

qs.e: There's no TV.
qs.t: What is NOT in Ken's room?

qs.e: There's no elevator.
qs.t: What problem does Ken have?

mr030.tt:
This is a composition written by Lee.

Fireworks
Lee

In August I went to see fireworks with friends. There were so many people between the station and the river that it took us a whole 30 minutes.
The fireworks started at 7:30 p.m. There were lots of big, beautiful fireworks.
But on the way home, the train was very crowded. We waited for an hour at a café near the station and then went home.

qs.e: There were a lot of people.
qs.t: Why did it take so long from the station to the river?

qs.e: They waited at the café.
qs.t: What did Lee and his friends do after the fireworks?
